message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical, Chemical, and Nuclear Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium, 99.98 %), H‑2 (deuterium, 0.02 %), H‑3 (tritium, trace) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, so it does not readily accept an electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µB (protium) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high (≈0.61 cm² s⁻¹ at 25 °C) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ (≈0.0008 % by volume) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Bond type | Diatomic (H₂) |
| | Molecular weight | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ |
| | Flammability | Highly flammable; explosive range 4–75 % in air |
| | Reactivity | Forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂), reacts with halogens (HX), oxidizes to water or oxides, participates in acid–base chemistry as a proton donor (H⁺) |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a proton donor (acidic) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) |
| | Redox behavior | Can be reduced to metal (protium) or oxidized to water/oxides; participates in hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) |
| | Spectroscopic features | Strong absorption in UV (Lyman series), infrared (vibrational stretching ~4400 cm⁻¹), microwave rotational transitions (~1420 MHz for 21‑cm line) |
| **Nuclear & Isotopic Features** | Deuterium (²H) | Stable isotope, used in heavy water (D₂O) and nuclear fusion research |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (β⁻ decay, half‑life ≈12.32 yr), used in nuclear weapons and fusion experiments |
| | Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) | ¹H NMR is a cornerstone analytical technique; chemical shift range ~0–10 ppm |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel | Hydrogen fuel cells (producing electricity + water) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen (LH₂/LOX) |
| | Industrial | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Scientific | Calibration standards, tracer studies, neutron sources (via deuterium) |
| | Medical | MRI contrast agents (deuterated compounds), PET imaging (tritium-labeled tracers) |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: lowest density, high diffusivity, and very low boiling/melting points.
- **Highly reactive**: forms a wide variety of compounds (hydrides, acids, organohydrogens).
- **Isotopic diversity**: protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavy water), tritium (radioactive, fusion).
- **Key role in energy**: central to fuel cells, rocket propulsion, and potential fusion power.
- **Spectroscopic importance**: ¹H NMR is ubiquitous in chemistry; the 21‑cm hydrogen line is fundamental in radio astronomy.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
